title: Descent of finite field towers along an algebraic union
statement: Let $A\subseteq M\subseteq\Omega$ be fields [def-weil-field] with $M/A$ algebraic (each element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $A$). Let $B\subseteq\Omega$ be a field containing $A$, finite-dimensional over $A$, and let $BM$ denote the smallest subfield of $\Omega$ containing $B$ and $M$. Given a finite tower of intermediate fields $$M=F_0\subseteq F_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_n=BM,$$ there exist an intermediate field $A\subseteq A_0\subseteq M$, finite-dimensional over $A$, and fields $$A_0=E_0\subseteq E_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq E_n=BA_0\subseteq BM$$ such that $ME_i=F_i$ for all $i$ and $[E_{i+1}:E_i]=[F_{i+1}:F_i]$ for every $0\le i<n$. Identity steps and $n=0$ are allowed. All composita are taken inside $\Omega$, and every displayed degree is vector-space dimension.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49, the inference from a tower over the maximal tame extension to a finite moderately ramified base; explicit algebraic finite-data formulation by NB.

proof.text: If $n=0$, then $BM=M$, hence $B\subseteq M$. Take $A_0=E_0=B$. This is finite over $A$, and $ME_0=M=F_0$; there are no degree conditions. Henceforth assume $n\ge1$. Choose a finite spanning family for the $A$-vector space $B$ (given by finite-dimensionality), and apply [lem-weil-span-independent-subfamily] to extract an $A$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ of $B$. Here $s\ge1$ since $1\ne0$ in $B$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49: agent-written finite-data expansion, zero-length case and finite generating data

proof.text: Inside $\Omega$ put $V=\{\sum_{j=1}^s m_jb_j:m_j\in M\}$. Every product $b_jb_k$ and $1$ is an $A$-linear combination of the $b_l$, since these form an $A$-basis of the field $B$. Thus $V$ is closed under multiplication, contains $1$, and is a commutative $M$-algebra of dimension at most $s$. It is an integral domain, being a subring of the field $\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], $V$ is a field. It contains $M$ and $B$, so $BM\subseteq V$ by the defining minimality of the compositum. Conversely each displayed sum belongs to $BM$. Therefore $BM=V$; in particular $BM/M$ has a finite spanning family consisting of elements of $B$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49: agent-written finite-data expansion, finite span equals the compositum

proof.text: Choose finite $M$-bases $v_i=(v_{i,1},\ldots,v_{i,d_i})$ for all $F_i$, taking $v_0=(1)$. Here is a bounded construction for the intervening fields: start with the empty independent family in $F_i$ and append an element outside its span whenever it does not yet span $F_i$. Appending preserves independence, since a relation with nonzero new coefficient would put that element in the old span. Every such family is also independent in $BM$, so [lem-sfb-independent-family-spanning-cardinality], applied over $M$ to the spanning set $\{b_1,\ldots,b_s\}$ of $BM$, bounds its length by $s$. Hence after at most $s$ additions it spans $F_i$. For $F_n=BM$ specifically use [lem-weil-span-independent-subfamily] on $b_1,\ldots,b_s$ over $M$; this chooses $v_n$ from that family, so each $v_{n,j}$ lies in $B$. Each $d_i\ge1$ because $1\in F_i$ is nonzero.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49: agent-written finite-data expansion, finite bases, with the last basis chosen inside B

proof.text: Write the following finitely many identities in these bases, with coefficients in $M$: for every $i$, the expansion of $1$ in $v_i$ and of each $v_{i,j}v_{i,k}$ in $v_i$; for $i<n$, the expansion of each $v_{i,j}$ in $v_{i+1}$; and the expansion of each $b_j$ in $v_n$. Let $C\subseteq M$ be the union of all coefficients appearing in these identities, and let $A_0=A(C)\subseteq M$ be the subfield generated by $A$ and $C$. There are only finitely many indices and every basis is finite, so $C$ is finite. Each of its elements is algebraic over $A$ by the hypothesis on $M/A$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] to precisely this finite set proves $[A_0:A]<\infty$. Every recorded identity now has coefficients in $A_0$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49: agent-written finite-data expansion, one finite coefficient field (Stacks Tag 09GH, fields-lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated)

proof.text: For each $i$ set $E_i=\{\sum_{j=1}^{d_i} a_jv_{i,j}:a_j\in A_0\}\subseteq F_i$. The recorded identity for $1$ shows $1\in E_i$, hence $A_0\subseteq E_i$. The multiplication identities show that the product of any two displayed sums is again such a sum. Addition and additive inverses are closed by the same formula. Thus $E_i$ is a commutative finite-dimensional $A_0$-algebra and a nonzero domain inside $\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], it is a field. Moreover $v_i$ is independent over $A_0$: an $A_0$-linear relation is an $M$-linear relation because $A_0\subseteq M$, and its coefficients vanish by the chosen $M$-basis property. Therefore $v_i$ is an $A_0$-basis of $E_i$, so $[E_i:A_0]=d_i=[F_i:M]$ by [def-weil-vector-space-dimension].

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49: agent-written finite-data expansion, multiplication tables produce actual fields with the chosen bases

proof.text: The recorded inclusion identities imply $E_i\subseteq E_{i+1}$: substitute the $A_0$-linear expansion of each $v_{i,j}$ into any $A_0$-linear combination. Since $v_0=(1)$, $E_0=A_0$. At the other endpoint, $v_n\subseteq B$ implies $E_n\subseteq BA_0$. Conversely all $b_j$ belong to $E_n$ by their recorded expansions. Since $E_n$ is a field containing $A_0\supseteq A$, it then contains every $A$-linear combination of the $b_j$, hence all of $B$. The minimality of the compositum gives $BA_0\subseteq E_n$. Thus $E_n=BA_0$. All these fields lie inside $BM$ by construction.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49: agent-written finite-data expansion, the nested tower and its two endpoints

proof.text: For every $i$, the field $ME_i$ is contained in $F_i$ because $M,E_i\subseteq F_i$. Conversely $ME_i$ contains every $v_{i,j}$ and every coefficient in $M$, so it contains every $M$-linear combination of $v_i$, namely all of $F_i$. Thus $ME_i=F_i$ for every $i$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49: agent-written finite-data expansion, recovery after taking the compositum with M

proof.text: For $i<n$, the finite family $v_{i+1}$ spans $E_{i+1}$ over $E_i$, because it already spans over $A_0\subseteq E_i$. It also spans $F_{i+1}$ over $F_i$, because it already spans over $M\subseteq F_i$. Thus both successive extensions are finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] to $A_0\subseteq E_i\subseteq E_{i+1}$ and to $M\subseteq F_i\subseteq F_{i+1}$. Using the basis cardinalities from step 5 gives $d_i[E_{i+1}:E_i]=d_{i+1}=d_i[F_{i+1}:F_i]$. As $d_i\ge1$, cancellation in the natural numbers gives the required equality of successive degrees. No step required a strict inclusion, so identity steps are included.

It is the algebraic form of the inference 'there exists a finite moderately ramified K' with K'L/K' split into p-steps' in Temkin 0707.3953v3, first paragraph of the proof of Thm 6.3.1, printed p. 49. The local PDF is absent, so I read the author's PDF from source.url via pdftotext in /tmp. The parent lem-trf-valued-tame-prime-tower uses the item with M=T, B=D, which matches the hypotheses, and the item does not restate the parent. All eight steps check. (1) n=0: B⊆M, A_0=B; A-basis of B by lem-weil-span-independent-subfamily. (2) BM is the M-span of the b_j, a field by lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field; its algebra and domain hypotheses are checked in the step. (3) M-bases v_i, length bounded by lem-sfb-independent-family-spanning-cardinality; v_n is chosen inside B and v_0=(1). (4) The finite coefficient set (units, multiplication tables, inclusions, b_j) generates A_0, finite over A by lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension. (5) E_i, the A_0-span of v_i, is a field of degree d_i over A_0. (6)-(7) Elementary inclusions give E_n=BA_0 and ME_i=F_i. (8) Degree multiplicativity and cancellation since d_i≥1. Edge cases tested: n=0, identity steps with B⊆M, Q(√2,√3,…) with B=Q(2^{1/4}), algebraically closed M, inseparable towers. No new nodes. The DAG search found no duplicate and there is no re-split repair note. The added stmt_deps are justified. No fixes and no tool_uses.
